Record cards expose source-native values under their original column names.

sampling context together.

L2 adds related experimental records for the same molecule and exact condition.

may not generalize. Permeability, solubility, or mechanism alone is not a direct
oral-bioavailability outcome.

records did not define the accepted gold outcome: never count them as extra gold
votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

parent-condition context may apply to the query. It is not a positive-class
probability, an experimental result, or a substitute for reasoning about the
visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: Ipratropium, a quaternary ammonium anticholinergic, has absolute oral bioavailability of about 2-3% in healthy volunteers across 2-20 mg oral doses, with low bioavailability partly attributed to active intestinal secretion; this is the most transferable context for the query's quaternary ammonium.

Physostigmine, an N-methyl indoline alkaloid, has low oral bioavailability in healthy volunteers (3% oral solution, 1-2%, 3-8%, <1%, 1 to <5%) and ~2% in rats, although some patient studies report ~25%; the query's N-methyl indoline moiety is analogous.

The query contains a permanent quaternary ammonium and an N-methyl indoline, combining key absorption liabilities seen in ipratropium and physostigmine; the explicit positive charge undermines the high physicochemical prior.

L3 oral AUC/Cmax records concern unrelated reference molecules (tricyclic antidepressants, treprostinil, levomilnacipran, morphine, vinorelbine, granisetron, fentanyl, cariprazine, cocaine, etc.) and none report absolute oral bioavailability for a quaternary ammonium indoline alkaloid; they do not alter the low prediction.

evidence_gaps: No direct experimental oral bioavailability data for the query molecule.
The property tool reports neutral fraction 0.98 despite an explicit quaternary ammonium in the SMILES; this discrepancy is unresolved and the permanent charge is a major absorption liability.
Solubility/dissolution and first-pass metabolism of the query are unknown.
Transfer from ipratropium and physostigmine is analog-based, not direct.
L3 oral AUC/Cmax records are for unrelated molecules and do not provide query-specific F data.
Some higher F outliers in less transferable contexts (ipratropium 30%, physostigmine ~25% in patients) create uncertainty.
